key: Worship at dawn and instigate the Asvins: nor is the worshipper at eve rejected. Besides ourselves another craves and worships: each first in worship is most highly favoured.
s: In a hymn calling for the Asvins to be worshipped first, at daybreak, the verse presses the point; Sāyaṇa, on 5.77.2, reads the evening clause as saying the gods do not accept an evening offering, since scripture gives them the forenoon.

evidence.gloss: In the evening an oblation going to the gods does not exist: the gods do not accept it; it is unwelcome, not to be enjoyed. For the śruti says: ‘the forenoon indeed is the gods’. And if another than us sacrifices with Soma and satisfies them with oblation, then among us and others whoever sacrifices first is most to be favoured by the gods.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, 430/2). Sāyaṇa on 5.77.2 says an evening oblation does not go to the gods, they do not accept it, it is unwelcome, citing the śruti ‘the forenoon belongs to the gods’; Wilson translates him so and Griffith’s note marks it as Sāyaṇa’s reading against his own rendering. The sentence attributes the reading to him and does not resolve the difference with the translation. Plain sense fits the hymn (5.77.1 calls for the Asvins to be worshipped first, at dawn). Revision 209188 is 2019-08-11. entry-check ok.
